result.title: THG-Omni: Traceable Human-Centric Graph Supervision for Video Reasoning
result.summary: Omni-modal models can answer questions about video, but their predictions rarely show which participant, event, or interval supports an answer. Moreover, answer-level supervision alone does not teach a model to interpret structured video evidence. To systematically mitigate this issue, we present THG-Omni, a human-centric graph-supervision framework that links Segment Anything Model~3 participant tracks with temporally grounded Qwen3-VL annotations. Candidate semantic claims are checked against the source video and available audio before they are used to construct training questions, while track geometry provides explicit spatial and temporal supervision. The resulting questions teach an omni-modal reasoning model to interpret participant attributes, actions, affect, interactions, and their timing from a structured graph. At inference, THG-Omni uses a predicted graph constructed from the evaluation video. Experiments on IntentBench show consistent improvements over the unadapted backbone across social reasoning, emotion understanding, and deception perception. On NExT-QA, THG-Omni achieves 89.54\% accuracy with the matched graph, compared with 85.10\% without graph input. Further validation experiments show that compact graph input achieves 78.22\% accuracy, compared with 78.02\% using the full graph and 77.58\% without graph input. A complementary diagnostic demonstrates that the predicted graph preserves evidence useful for answering questions even without the source video and audio. Together, these findings show that THG-Omni improves human-centric video reasoning while grounding its evidence in identifiable participants and events. Our codes are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/review-n94hhfcwp5666/

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 THG-Omni，用人物中心图结构监督全模态视频推理：把参与者轨迹与带时间定位的标注连成图，构建可核查的训练问答，并在推理时使用预测图，使答案可追溯到具体参与者、事件与时间区间。
AI.relevance_reason: 其图结构是显式证据载体而非 latent 状态，但其「仅凭预测图仍保留答题所需证据」的诊断可供核查视觉细节与实体关系在内部表示中的保留与坍缩问题，并关联证据筛选与可追溯性评价。
